regions.text: 機械作用が原因となつて寶が地中に埋められた。

quote.translation: On the one hand, the mechanical action of A's spade was the cause of the treasure's being buried in the ground.

regions.text: 他方にば乙の織の機械作用が原因となつて土地が掘りかへされた。

quote.translation: On the other hand, the mechanical action of B's spade was the cause of the earth's being dug over.

regions.text: そこには二つの獨立な因果系列があつて、さうしてその二つの因果系列がたまたま一つの開係に置かれたのである。

quote.translation: There were two independent causal series, and these two causal series were placed by chance in a single relation.

regions.text: 要するに目的々横極偶然の根柢には因果積極的偶然が潜んでゐる。

quote.translation: In short, positive causal contingency lies hidden at the root of positive teleological contingency.

regions.text: 然るにここに一つの注日すべき現象がある。

quote.translation: Here, however, there is a phenomenon worth noting.

regions.text: さきに目的々偶然に「目釣なき目的」が件ふこと、目々消極偶然にあつてはその上肢たる「目なき」ことが强され、目々積極的偶然にあつてはその下肢たる「目約が强調されることを述べた。然るに目々偶然のこの性格は因果約積極的偶然へも反映されるのである。

quote.translation: We said earlier that teleological contingency is accompanied by a "purpose without purpose", and that in negative teleological contingency the first member of that phrase, "without purpose", is emphasised, whilst in positive teleological contingency the second member, "purpose", is emphasised.

regions.text: さうして因果的積極的偶然も一種の假想約な「目前なき目的」を有つこととなるのである。

quote.translation: This character of teleological contingency is reflected in positive causal contingency too, so that positive causal contingency also comes to have a kind of imagined "purpose without purpose".

regions.text: 屋根瓦が落ちて來てちやうどゴム風船に當つた事實の中には何等かいたづらな目前が隠されてるるかの如く火山の噴出と日蝕とが同時に起つたことの中には何等かの神秘な目的が溶んであるかの如くに感じられるのである。

quote.translation: When the roof tile fell and just hit the rubber balloon, we feel as though some mischievous purpose were hidden in it; when the volcano's eruption and the solar eclipse occurred at the same time, we feel as though some mysterious purpose lay behind them.

regions.text: 然しそれらは全く目前々偶然の「目的なき目的」を一種の感情移入によつて因果約積極偶然へ投射したに過ぎないのである。さうしてこ

quote.translation: These feelings, however, are nothing more than the projection, through a kind of empathy, of the "purpose without purpose" of teleological contingency onto positive causal contingency.

And from this standpoint we can also assert that the distinction between Aristotle's automaton and tychē is the distinction between positive causal contingency and positive teleological contingency (see p. 109).
